events.title: Birth of Benjamin Franklin
events.description: Benjamin Franklin was born in Boston, Massachusetts (January 17, 1706, New Style calendar). He became a printer, writer, scientist, inventor, diplomat, and one of the Founding Fathers of the United States.
events.significance: Franklin helped draft the Declaration of Independence, negotiated the Treaty of Paris and the French alliance, and made foundational discoveries about electricity, shaping both American independence and the Enlightenment.

events.title: Captain Cook Crosses the Antarctic Circle
events.description: During his second voyage, James Cook's ships HMS Resolution and HMS Adventure became the first known vessels to cross the Antarctic Circle.
events.significance: The voyage helped disprove the existence of a habitable southern continent and advanced knowledge of the polar regions and global navigation.

events.title: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Monarchy
events.description: A group of American and European businessmen and sugar planters, supported by US Marines, deposed Queen Liliuokalani and ended the rule of the Kingdom of Hawaii.
events.significance: The coup led to the establishment of the Republic of Hawaii and paved the way for US annexation in 1898, ending Hawaiian sovereignty.

events.title: Eisenhower's Farewell Address
events.description: President Dwight D. Eisenhower delivered his farewell address, warning Americans about the growing influence of the military-industrial complex.
events.significance: The speech remains one of the most cited presidential addresses, cautioning against unchecked military and industrial power in a democracy.

events.title: Operation Desert Storm Begins
events.description: A US-led coalition launched a massive air campaign against Iraq, beginning the Gulf War after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
events.significance: The war liberated Kuwait, demonstrated modern precision air power, and reshaped US involvement and geopolitics in the Middle East.
